title: Tanzanian Simit Bread Ring
community: Coastal Tanzania — the sesame bread ring
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Mkate wa Mviringo — a round bread ring coated in sesame seeds, lightly sweetened and baked until golden. The coastal Tanzanian bread ring sold at morning markets — the distant cousin of the Turkish simit, transformed by the Swahili coast.
longDesc: The sesame bread ring on the Tanzanian coast reflects the ancient connections between the Swahili coast and the Middle Eastern and Asian trading worlds. Sold at morning markets, it is the bread ring that workers and students buy on the way to the day's work.
ingredients: 1 tbsp honey mixed with 1 tbsp water for glazing
steps: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water. Rest 10 minutes.
Mix flour and salt. Add yeast mixture and oil. Knead 8 minutes.
Divide into 8. Roll each into a rope. Form into a ring. Pinch ends.
Dip in honey-water. Coat in sesame seeds.
Place on baking sheet. Rest 15 minutes.
Bake at 190°C for 18—20 minutes until golden.
chefTips: Honey-water dip makes the sesame seeds adhere.
Pinch the ring ends very firmly — they open during baking if poorly sealed.
cookingScience: The honey-water glaze serves as an adhesive for the sesame seeds — the sugars in honey are hygroscopic and slightly sticky, binding the sesame to the dough surface. During baking, the sugar caramelises, creating an even more robust bond.
sustainabilityTips: Locally grown sesame — Tanzania produces excellent sesame.
healthBenefits: Sesame seeds add calcium and zinc.
culturalNote: The sesame bread ring is the Tanzanian coast's connection to the ancient maritime world — the bread shape carried to East Africa on the same dhows that brought cloves and cardamom from the north.
